summary: Speculative workflow task processing lacks shard ownership verification, causing valid workflow update requests to be incorrectly rejected when shard ownership changes during task execution. A fix requires exposing AssertShardOwnership through the ShardContext interface.
userImpact: Users experience silent rejections of valid workflow update requests when shard ownership changes during task execution, with no error logged to indicate the reason.
rootCause: ShardContext interface does not expose AssertShardOwnership method, preventing speculative workflow task processing from verifying shard ownership before completing and updating mutable state.
proposedFix: Expose AssertShardOwnership through ShardContext interface and call it in skipWorkflowTaskCompletedEvent before task completion. May require adding context parameter and changing return type to handle errors, updating all callers.
keyQuote: No shard ownership check is performed during speculative workflow task processing... causing valid workflow update requests to be incorrectly rejected with no error logged.
